title: Introduce minimal auth shim and ergonomic stream adapters with iterator sugar
author: Ethan Li
release_notes: Introduce a lightweight cross-SDK auth shim and ergonomic stream iterator helpers. Minor API deprecations announced; migration guide added. Version bumps: py->1.12.0, ts->3.8.0, go->1.5.0.
description: Motivation: SDK users frequently asked for a smaller surface for credential handling that is easy to adopt in quickstart flows while preserving advanced extension points for platform teams; streaming ergonomics varied across languages which led to frequent copy-paste adapters. This PR introduces a minimal, implementation-agnostic credential shim (CredentialShim) and a thin StreamIterator sugar layer that unifies common patterns across Python/TypeScript/Go; it keeps full feature parity for existing advanced credential adapters. Goals: reduce onboarding friction for simple uses, keep opt-in behavior for credential caching, and provide a single ergonomic pattern for async streaming consumers. Changes (high-level): 1) New cross-language contract: CredentialShim (stateless helper + optional decorator) implemented in sdk/python, sdk/typescript, sdk/go; 2) StreamIterator sugar: buffering + automatic backpressure hinting + easy checkpoint() method to surface resume tokens; 3) Deprecation: verbose token lifecycle helpers are marked deprecated with stable replacement examples in docs; 4) Version bumps in each SDK to signal ergonomics upgrade (Python 1.12.0, TypeScript 3.8.0, Go 1.5.0); 5) Examples and migration guide under docs/sdk/migration/minimal-cred-shim.md; 6) Integration tests and e2e smoke for bearer rotation and long-lived streams. Implementation notes: the shim is intentionally small (~80 LOC per SDK) and exposes two entrypoints: wrap_handler(handler) and get_token(context) where get_token delegates to underlying credential providers if present. StreamIterator is a tiny adapter on top of existing pull/push stream primitives and adds a uniform async iterator/for-await-of/chan-style interface across languages. Performance: synthetic microbenchmarks show median 0.6ms added overhead on cold auth-paths; warm paths (cached token) show negligible delta. Testing: unit tests for shim behavior (rotation, error propagation), cross-SDK e2e that replays a long stream while rotating tokens to validate resume behavior. Migration: docs include a short recipe and a linter rule to flag deprecated helpers. Rollout: feature flagged to opt-in via SDK config; no immediate runtime changes for existing users. Backwards compatibility: default behavior mirrors previous token lookup semantics; credential caching must be explicitly enabled to avoid surprising stateful behavior in short-lived apps. Checklist: [x] design doc referenced (ENG-8792) [x] API sketches reviewed by DX and Go teams [x] unit + integration tests added [x] docs and migration guide added [x] CI green after fixup commit. Why this is different: instead of another large credential orchestrator, this focuses on a minimal, discoverable surface for application developers while keeping the full credential orchestration pluggable for platform/product integrations.

notes: This change is intentionally backward-compatible by default; teams that want credential caching or advanced orchestration should opt into the new shim or continue using existing adapters. Support notified via SUP-1420. Expect SDK minor version bumps in next release cadence.
